# Wrapcheck

A simple Go linter to check that errors from external packages are wrapped
during return to help identify the error source during debugging.

## What is Wrapcheck?

Wrapcheck is a linter that checks whether errors from external packages are
wrapped when returned. This helps identify error sources during debugging by
adding context at package boundaries.

## Installation

Go >= v1.22.0
```bash
$ go install github.com/tomarrell/wrapcheck/v2/cmd/wrapcheck@v2
```

Wrapcheck is also available as part of the golangci-lint meta linter.

## Usage

To lint all the packages in a program:

```bash
$ wrapcheck ./...
```

## Configuration

You can configure wrapcheck by using a `.wrapcheck.yaml` file in either the
local directory, or in your home directory.

```yaml
# An array of strings which specify substrings of signatures to ignore. If this
# set, it will override the default set of ignored signatures.
ignoreSigs:
- .Errorf(
- errors.New(
- errors.Unwrap(
- errors.Join(
- .Wrap(
- .Wrapf(
- .WithMessage(
- .WithMessagef(
- .WithStack(

# An array of strings specifying additional substrings of signatures to ignore.
# Unlike ignoreSigs, this option extends the default set (or the set specified
# in ignoreSigs) without replacing it entirely.
extraIgnoreSigs:
- .CustomError(
- .SpecificWrap(

# An array of strings which specify regular expressions of signatures to ignore.
ignoreSigRegexps:
- \.New.*Error\(

# An array of glob patterns which, if any match the package of the function
# returning the error, will skip wrapcheck analysis for this error.
ignorePackageGlobs:
- encoding/*
- github.com/pkg/*

# ignoreInterfaceRegexps defines a list of regular expressions which, if matched
# to a underlying interface name, will ignore unwrapped errors returned from a
# function whose call is defined on the given interface.
ignoreInterfaceRegexps:
- ^(?i)c(?-i)ach(ing|e)

# ReportInternalErrors determines whether wrapcheck should report errors returned
# from inside the package.
reportInternalErrors: true
```

## Example

If you've ever been debugging your Go program and seen an error like this:

```log
time="2020-08-04T11:36:27+02:00" level=error error="sql: error no rows"
```

Then you know how painful it can be to hunt down the cause when you have
many methods that return errors from the same external package.

The problem is that multiple method calls into external packages (like `sql`)
can return the same error. Wrapcheck helps you enforce wrapping errors at
package boundaries to add context.

### Before (unwrapped errors)

```go
func (db *DB) getUserByID(userID string) (User, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = $1;`

    var u User
    if err := db.conn.Get(&u, sql, userID); err != nil {
        return User{}, err // wrapcheck error: error returned from external package is unwrapped
    }

    return u, nil
}

func (db *DB) getItemByID(itemID string) (Item, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM item WHERE id = $1;`

    var i Item
    if err := db.conn.Get(&i, sql, itemID); err != nil {
        return Item{}, err // wrapcheck error: error returned from external package is unwrapped
    }

    return i, nil
}
```

### After (wrapped errors)

```go
func (db *DB) getUserByID(userID string) (User, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM user WHERE id = $1;`

    var u User
    if err := db.Conn.Get(&u, sql, userID); err != nil {
        return User{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get user by ID: %v", err) // No error!
    }

    return u, nil
}

func (db *DB) getItemByID(itemID string) (Item, error) {
    sql := `SELECT * FROM item WHERE id = $1;`

    var i Item
    if err := db.Conn.Get(&i, sql, itemID); err != nil {
        return Item{}, fmt.Errorf("failed to get item by ID: %v", err) // No error!
    }

    return i, nil
}
```

Now, your logs will be more descriptive:

```log
time="2020-08-04T11:36:27+02:00" level=error error="failed to get user by ID: sql: error no rows"
```

## Why Wrap Errors?

Errors in Go are simple values that contain only an error message. When you
call external libraries which may return errors, wrapping the error at the
call site adds additional information about where the error occurred. This
makes debugging much easier, especially when multiple calls to the same
library can return the same error.

As of Go 1.13, error wrapping using `fmt.Errorf(...)` is the recommended way
to compose errors in Go to add additional information.

import subprocess, os, textwrap, shutil, pathlib, sys
EXE="/workspace/executable"
BASE=pathlib.Path("/tmp/wtprobe")
def setup():
    if BASE.exists(): shutil.rmtree(BASE)
    (BASE/"bar").mkdir(parents=True)
    (BASE/"bar"/"bar.go").write_text(textwrap.dedent('''
        package bar
        import "errors"
        var ErrBar = errors.New("bar var")
        func Do() error { return errors.New("bar") }
        func Do2() (int, error) { return 0, errors.New("x") }
        func Wrap(err error, msg string) error { return err }
        func Wrapf(err error, format string, args ...interface{}) error { return err }
        func Custom(err error) error { return err }
        type S struct{}
        func (S) Method() error { return errors.New("m") }
        func (S) Wrap(err error) error { return err }
        type Iface interface { DoIface() error }
        '''))
    (BASE/"go.mod").write_text("module example.com/wtprobe\ngo 1.21\n")
def run(code, extra_files=None, config=None, args=None, cwd=None):
    setup()
    (BASE/"main.go").write_text(code)
    if extra_files:
        for k,v in extra_files.items():
            p=BASE/k; p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); p.write_text(v)
    # clean config in home? check
    if config is not None:
        (BASE/".wrapcheck.yaml").write_text(config)
    else:
        # ensure no leftover
        pass
    cmd=[EXE]+(args or ["./..."])
    env=os.environ.copy()
    # isolate HOME to empty dir unless config test
    home="/tmp/fakehome"
    os.makedirs(home, exist_ok=True)
    for f in os.listdir(home):
        try: os.remove(os.path.join(home,f))
        except: pass
    env["HOME"]=home
    result=subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd or BASE, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    # strip base path
    out=result.stdout+result.stderr
    out=out.replace(str(BASE)+"/","")
    print(out, end="")
    if result.returncode!=0:
        print(f"[exit {result.returncode}]")
    print("---")
    return result

if __name__=="__main__":
    pass

    setup(); p=BASE/(".wrapcheck."+ext if ext else ".wrapcheck"); p.write_text("ignoreSigs: []\n"); print(repr(ext), run())
# chain order test: put good in first and bad in second, if first wins exit3 if second wins exit1 ; do chain in observed guessed order sequentially pairs

for a,b in zip(order, order[1:]):

    (BASE/(".wrapcheck."+a if a else ".wrapcheck")).write_text("ignoreSigs: []\n")

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"go/ast"
	"go/types"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis"
	"golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/inspect"
	"golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/singlechecker"
)

func main() {
	singlechecker.Main(newAnalyzer())
}

func newAnalyzer() *analysis.Analyzer {
	cfg := loadConfig()

	return &analysis.Analyzer{
		Name:     "wrapcheck",
		Doc:      "Checks that errors returned from external packages are wrapped",
		Requires: []*analysis.Analyzer{inspect.Analyzer},
		Run: func(pass *analysis.Pass) (interface{}, error) {
			return run(pass, cfg)
		},
	}
}

type compiledConfig struct {
	cfg              *wrapConfig
	sigRegexps       []*regexp.Regexp
	interfaceRegexps []*regexp.Regexp
	packageGlobs     []globMatcher
}

func compileConfig(cfg *wrapConfig) (*compiledConfig, error) {
	cc := &compiledConfig{cfg: cfg}

	for _, pattern := range cfg.IgnoreSigRegexps {
		re, err := regexp.Compile(pattern)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to compile regexp %s: %w", pattern, err)
		}
		cc.sigRegexps = append(cc.sigRegexps, re)
	}

	for _, pattern := range cfg.IgnoreInterfaceRegexps {
		re, err := regexp.Compile(pattern)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to compile regexp %s: %w", pattern, err)
		}
		cc.interfaceRegexps = append(cc.interfaceRegexps, re)
	}

	for _, pattern := range cfg.IgnorePackageGlobs {
		g, err := compileGlob(pattern)
		if err != nil {
			var compiled interface{}
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to compile globs %s: %w", compiled, err)
		}
		cc.packageGlobs = append(cc.packageGlobs, g)
	}

	return cc, nil
}

func run(pass *analysis.Pass, cfg *wrapConfig) (interface{}, error) {
	cc, err := compileConfig(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	for _, file := range pass.Files {
		assignments := collectValueSpecs(pass, file)

		// stack contains the ancestors of the node currently being visited.
		// ast.Inspect calls the callback with nil after each node's children.
		var stack []ast.Node
		ast.Inspect(file, func(node ast.Node) bool {
			if node == nil {
				if len(stack) > 0 {
					stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
				}
				return true
			}

			switch n := node.(type) {
			case *ast.AssignStmt:
				recordAssignment(pass, assignments, n)
			case *ast.ReturnStmt:
				checkReturn(pass, cc, assignments, stack, n)
			}

			stack = append(stack, node)
			return true
		})
	}

	return nil, nil
}

	ast.Inspect(file, func(node ast.Node) bool {
		spec, ok := node.(*ast.ValueSpec)
		if !ok || len(spec.Values) == 0 {
			return true
		}
		call, isCall := spec.Values[0].(*ast.CallExpr)
		for _, name := range spec.Names {

				continue
			}
			obj := pass.TypesInfo.ObjectOf(name)
			if obj == nil {
				continue
			}

				assignments[obj] = nil

	for _, lhs := range assign.Lhs {

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"go/ast"
	"go/token"
	"go/types"
	"regexp"
	"strings"

	"golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis"
	"golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/passes/inspect"
	"golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis/singlechecker"
)

func main() {
	singlechecker.Main(newAnalyzer())
}

func newAnalyzer() *analysis.Analyzer {
	cfg := loadConfig()

	return &analysis.Analyzer{
		Name:     "wrapcheck",
		Doc:      "Checks that errors returned from external packages are wrapped",
		Requires: []*analysis.Analyzer{inspect.Analyzer},
		Run: func(pass *analysis.Pass) (interface{}, error) {
			return run(pass, cfg)
		},
	}
}

type compiledConfig struct {
	cfg              *wrapConfig
	sigRegexps       []*regexp.Regexp
	interfaceRegexps []*regexp.Regexp
	packageGlobs     []globMatcher
}

func compileConfig(cfg *wrapConfig) (*compiledConfig, error) {
	cc := &compiledConfig{cfg: cfg}

	for _, pattern := range cfg.IgnoreSigRegexps {
		re, err := regexp.Compile(pattern)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to compile regexp %s: %w\n", pattern, err)
		}
		cc.sigRegexps = append(cc.sigRegexps, re)
	}

	for _, pattern := range cfg.IgnoreInterfaceRegexps {
		re, err := regexp.Compile(pattern)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to compile regexp %s: %w\n", pattern, err)
		}
		cc.interfaceRegexps = append(cc.interfaceRegexps, re)
	}

	for _, pattern := range cfg.IgnorePackageGlobs {
		g, err := compileGlob(pattern)
		if err != nil {
			var compiled interface{}
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unable to compile globs %s: %w\n", compiled, err)
		}
		cc.packageGlobs = append(cc.packageGlobs, g)
	}

	return cc, nil
}

func run(pass *analysis.Pass, cfg *wrapConfig) (interface{}, error) {
	cc, err := compileConfig(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	for _, file := range pass.Files {
		assignments := collectValueSpecs(pass, file)

		// stack contains the ancestors of the node currently being visited.
		// ast.Inspect calls the callback with nil after each node's children.
		var stack []ast.Node
		ast.Inspect(file, func(node ast.Node) bool {
			if node == nil {
				if len(stack) > 0 {
					stack = stack[:len(stack)-1]
				}
				return true
			}

			switch n := node.(type) {
			case *ast.AssignStmt:
				recordAssignment(pass, assignments, n)
			case *ast.ReturnStmt:
				checkReturn(pass, cc, assignments, stack, n)
			}

			stack = append(stack, node)
			return true
		})
	}

	return nil, nil
}

func collectValueSpecs(pass *analysis.Pass, file *ast.File) map[types.Object]*ast.CallExpr {
	assignments := make(map[types.Object]*ast.CallExpr)
	if pass.TypesInfo == nil {
		return assignments
	}
	ast.Inspect(file, func(node ast.Node) bool {
		spec, ok := node.(*ast.ValueSpec)
		if !ok || len(spec.Values) == 0 {
			return true
		}
		call, isCall := spec.Values[0].(*ast.CallExpr)
		for _, name := range spec.Names {
			if name == nil || name.Name == "_" {
				continue
			}
			obj := pass.TypesInfo.ObjectOf(name)
			if obj == nil {
				continue
			}
			if isCall {
				assignments[obj] = call
			} else {
				assignments[obj] = nil
			}
		}
		return true
	})
	return assignments
}

func recordAssignment(pass *analysis.Pass, assignments map[types.Object]*ast.CallExpr, assign *ast.AssignStmt) {
	if pass.TypesInfo == nil || len(assign.Rhs) == 0 {
		return
	}
	call, isCall := assign.Rhs[0].(*ast.CallExpr)
	for _, lhs := range assign.Lhs {
		ident, ok := lhs.(*ast.Ident)
		if !ok || ident.Name == "_" {
			continue
		}
		obj := pass.TypesInfo.ObjectOf(ident)
		if obj == nil {
			continue
		}
		if isCall {
			assignments[obj] = call
		} else {
			assignments[obj] = nil
		}
	}
}

func enclosingFunctionIsLiteral(stack []ast.Node) bool {
	for i := len(stack) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		switch stack[i].(type) {
		case *ast.FuncLit:
			return true
		case *ast.FuncDecl:
			return false
		}
	}
	return false
}

func checkReturn(pass *analysis.Pass, cc *compiledConfig, assignments map[types.Object]*ast.CallExpr, stack []ast.Node, ret *ast.ReturnStmt) {
	if pass.TypesInfo == nil {
		return
	}
	inLiteral := enclosingFunctionIsLiteral(stack)
	for _, result := range ret.Results {
		switch expr := result.(type) {
		case *ast.Ident:
			typ := pass.TypesInfo.TypeOf(expr)
			if typ == nil || typ.String() != "error" {
				continue
			}

		}

func calledObject(pass *analysis.Pass, call *ast.CallExpr) types.Object {

		return nil
	}
}

func isInterfaceType(typ types.Type) bool {

// lowerCaseKeys recursively lower-cases mapping keys. Configuration keys
// are therefore matched case-insensitively, including in nested values.
func lowerCaseKeys(v interface{}) interface{} {
	switch value := v.(type) {

	default:
